words.gloss: of the acquisitions of ally, money and land

hindi: संहित प्रयाण में मित्र, धन और भूमि के लाभों में से उत्तरोत्तर लाभ श्रेष्ठ है।
english: In a march in alliance, of the acquisitions of ally, money and land, each succeeding acquisition [is] better.
notes: saṃhita-prayāṇa taken literally as a march made allied or joined; the text does not say with whom. hiraṇya = money (glossary 5.2). uttara.uttaraḥ read as the repeated compound 'each later one'. mitra-hiraṇya-bhūmi-lābhānām: lābha = acquisition (Book 7 chapter on acquisitions); the dvandva is of the three things acquired.

hindi: क्योंकि मित्र और धन भूमि के लाभ से होते हैं, मित्र धन के लाभ से।
english: For ally and money arise from the acquisition of land, ally from the acquisition of money.
notes: Second clause has no verb; bhavataḥ is understood. 'Arise' for bhavataḥ is literal 'become/come to be'.

hindi: अथवा जो लाभ सिद्ध हुआ, शेष दोनों में से किसी एक को साधता है।
english: Or whichever acquisition, accomplished, accomplishes one of the remaining two.
notes: sādhayati (caus. √sādh) rendered 'accomplishes'; the sense 'brings about / secures' is the same. Hindi leaves the correlative unstated because the Sanskrit has no tad here (saḥ is absent).

words.gloss: having this as its beginning, and so on

hindi: “तुम और मैं मित्र प्राप्त करते हैं”, इस प्रकार आदि वाली सम सन्धि है।
english: “You and I obtain an ally”, [that] which has this as its beginning is an even treaty.

text_flags.why: possible: stray h for visarga (ādiḥ); the next word begins with s, and unit 5 reads evaṃ.ādir

notes: sama-sandhi = even treaty (glossary: sandhi = treaty; sama/viṣama = even/uneven as in 10.5). labhāvahe is a 1 du. present middle (the imperative would be labhāvahai). The closing iti of the quotation is carried by the quotation marks.

words.gloss: having this as its beginning, and so on

hindi: “तुम मित्र”, इस प्रकार आदि वाली विषम सन्धि है।
english: “You [are] an ally”, [that] which has this as its beginning is an uneven treaty.
notes: The quotation tvaṃ mitram has no verb; '[are]' is a bare copula. It could also be read 'you [obtain] an ally', or mitram as accusative, but the text gives no verb. The printed 'ādir viṣama' is regular sandhi for ādiḥ viṣama.

hindi: उन दोनों के विशेष लाभ से अतिसन्धि है।
english: From a special acquisition of those two, [there is] atisandhi.
notes: atisandhi kept as the term (literally 'over-treaty'); the sense 'outwitting' follows from atisandhatte in the next unit (cf. glossary atisandhā = outwit). tayoḥ taken as 'of the two (treaties)'; locative 'in the two' is also possible. Verb not stated.

hindi: किन्तु सम सन्धि में जो उत्कृष्ट मित्र अथवा मित्र के संकट में मित्र प्राप्त करता है, वह छल लेता है।
english: But in an even treaty, he who obtains an excellent ally, or an ally in an ally's difficulty, outwits [the other].
notes: sampanna = literally 'endowed, accomplished'; 'excellent' chosen (cf. unit 38 sampannaṃ mitraṃ ṣaḍ-guṇam). The object of atisandhatte is not stated. The printed 'so 'tisandhatte' = saḥ atisandhatte.

hindi: क्योंकि आपत्ति सौहार्द की स्थिरता उत्पन्न करती है।
english: For adversity produces steadiness of friendship.
notes: The printed 'āpadd hi' (doubled d) is the edition's regular spelling for āpad hi (the same occurs in 'tadd hi', unit 9); not flagged.

words.gram: n. nom. sg. pres. part. an-upa-√kṛ

hindi: मित्र के संकट में भी नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला, अथवा अनित्य, वश में रहने वाला — “नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला श्रेष्ठ है, क्योंकि वह उपकार न करता हुआ भी अपकार नहीं करता,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: Even in an ally's difficulty, a constant, uncontrolled [ally] or an inconstant, controlled one — “The constant, uncontrolled [one] is better, for it does not harm even when not helping,” say the teachers.
notes: The first iti (after vā) closes the either-or question; it is not rendered, the dash marks it. No noun is stated in the quotation. avaśya = not under control (a-vaśya), not Hindi 'certainly'; vaśya = under control. 'tadd hi' is the edition's regular spelling for tad dhi/tad hi.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: वश में रहने वाला अनित्य श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The controlled, inconstant [one] is better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).

hindi: जब तक उपकार करता है, तब तक मित्र होता है; मित्र उपकार के लक्षण वाला है।
english: As long as [it] helps, for so long [it] is an ally; an ally [is] one having help as its mark.
notes: The subject of upakaroti is not stated (the controlled ally of unit 11). The closing iti after 'mitram' is an explanatory close of a definition; not rendered, glossed closing particle.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. upa-√kṛ

hindi: दोनों वश में रहने वालों में भी महान् भोग वाला अनित्य, अथवा अल्प भोग वाला नित्य — “महान् भोग वाला अनित्य श्रेष्ठ है, महान् भोग वाला अनित्य थोड़े समय में बड़ा उपकार करता हुआ व्यय के बड़े स्थानों का प्रतिकार करता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: Even among two controlled [allies], one of great enjoyment, inconstant, or one of small enjoyment, constant — “The one of great enjoyment, inconstant, is better; the one of great enjoyment, inconstant, helping greatly in a short time, remedies the great occasions of expenditure,” say the teachers.
notes: bhoga rendered literally 'enjoyment'; 'use, yield, extent of benefit' are possible (cf. glossary 3.8 bhoga = use). vyaya-sthāna = literally 'places/occasions of expenditure'. mahad-upakurvan: mahat is taken as adverbial/object 'greatly', both give the same sense. Sense of the either-or question closed by the first iti; not rendered.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: नित्य, अल्प भोग वाला श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The constant [one] of small enjoyment is better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).

hindi: महान् भोग वाला अनित्य उपकार के भय से हट जाता है, अथवा उपकार करके वापस लेने का प्रयत्न करता है।
english: The inconstant [one] of great enjoyment goes away from fear of help, or, having helped, seeks to take back.
notes: upakāra-bhayāt is literally 'from fear of help'; whether the help is given or received is not stated. The object of pratyādātum is not stated.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. upa-√kṛ

hindi: नित्य, अल्प भोग वाला निरन्तरता से थोड़ा उपकार करता हुआ बड़े समय में बड़ा उपकार करता है।
english: The constant [one] of small enjoyment, through continuity, helping a little, helps greatly in a long time.
notes: mahatā kālena is the instrumental of time, 'in/over a long time'.

hindi: भारी रूप से उठने वाला महान् मित्र अथवा हल्के रूप से उठने वाला अल्प — “भारी रूप से उठने वाला महान् मित्र प्रताप उत्पन्न करने वाला होता है, और जब उठता है तब कार्य साधता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: A great ally of heavy rising or a small one of light rising — “A great ally of heavy rising is a producer of might, and when [it] rises, then [it] accomplishes the task,” say the teachers.
notes: guru-samuttha / laghu-samuttha taken literally 'heavy-rising / light-rising' (i.e. slow or quick to rise, to take the field); the text does not say more. pratāpa = might, majesty. The first iti closes the either-or question; not rendered.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: हल्के रूप से उठने वाला अल्प श्रेष्ठ है।
english: The small [one] of light rising is better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[one]' is understood (the ally).

hindi: हल्के रूप से उठने वाला अल्प मित्र कार्य के समय को निकलने नहीं देता, और दुर्बलता से इच्छानुसार उपभोग्य होता है, दूसरा नहीं, प्रकृष्ट भूमि वाला।
english: The small ally of light rising does not let the time of the task pass, and from weakness becomes [one] to be used as desired; not the other, [the one] of extensive territory.

text_flags.why: laghu is the word elsewhere in this chunk (units 18, 20); lagu is a likely typo

notes: prakṛṣṭa-bhauma is obscure: prakṛṣṭa 'excellent, extended, distant' and bhauma 'of the land'; rendered 'of extensive territory', literal alternatives noted. The same word occurs in unit 47. 'Becomes' translates bhavati; the ablative daurbalyāt is 'from weakness'.

hindi: बिखरी हुई सेना वाला अथवा वश में न रहने वाली सेना वाला — “बिखरी हुई सेना को वापस समेटा जा सकता है, वश में होने से,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: [An ally] having scattered troops or having uncontrolled troops — “Scattered troops can be drawn back, because of being under control,” say the teachers.
notes: The bahuvrīhis have no stated noun; '[ally]' is understood from the context of the chapter. śakyam pratisaṃhartum is 'possible to be drawn back'; the infinitive is used passively. The first iti closes the either-or question; not rendered.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: वश में न रहने वाली सेना वाला श्रेष्ठ है।
english: [The one] having uncontrolled troops is better.
notes: No noun is stated; '[the one]' is understood (the ally).

hindi: क्योंकि वश में न रहने वाले को साम आदि से वश में किया जा सकता है, दूसरा नहीं, कार्य में लगा हुआ, वापस समेटा जाने योग्य।
english: For the uncontrolled [one] can be made controlled by conciliation and the rest, not the other, engaged in a task, to be drawn back.
notes: 'Śakyam' is understood with the second clause (na itarat ... pratisaṃhartum): 'the other, engaged in a task, [cannot] be drawn back'. The translations keep the elliptic form. vyāsakta = engaged, absorbed (in a task).

hindi: पुरुषों में भोग वाला अथवा धन में भोग वाला मित्र — “पुरुषों में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है, पुरुषों में भोग वाला मित्र प्रताप उत्पन्न करने वाला होता है, और जब उठता है तब कार्य साधता है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: An ally of enjoyment in men or of enjoyment in money — “An ally of enjoyment in men is better; an ally of enjoyment in men is a producer of might, and when [it] rises, then [it] accomplishes the task,” say the teachers.

text_flags.why: likely typo: puruṣa is the word in the same quotation and in the first half of the unit; pruṣa is not a word

notes: puruṣa-bhoga is literally 'enjoyment (use) of men', understood as an ally whose enjoyment (benefit) consists of men; bhoga rendered as in unit 13. The first iti closes the either-or question and is not rendered.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: धन में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है।
english: An ally of enjoyment in money is better.

hindi: क्योंकि धन से जुड़ाव नित्य है, सेना से कभी-कभी।
english: For connection with money is constant, with the army sometimes.
notes: yoga is rendered 'connection' (joining), not the 6.2 'acquisition'. daṇḍa = army here (the prakṛti sense, glossary 6.2/8.5/9.7: army); no Book 7 line exists; 'force' or 'punishment' are not intended. The verb of the second clause is understood.

hindi: सेना और अन्य कामनाएँ धन से प्राप्त की जाती हैं।
english: Both the army and other desires are obtained by money.
notes: daṇḍa = army, as in unit 29 (note there). The two ca are rendered 'both ... and'. The closing iti completes the reason and is not rendered. Printed 'hiraṇyena-anye' is the '-' join of two words (hiraṇyena, anye).

words.gloss: causing the remedy of all expenditure

hindi: धन में भोग वाला अथवा भूमि में भोग वाला मित्र — “धन में भोग वाला, गतिमान् होने से, सब व्ययों का प्रतिकार करने वाला है,” ऐसा आचार्य कहते हैं।
english: An ally of enjoyment in money or of enjoyment in land — “[The ally] of enjoyment in money, because of having movement, is one who causes the remedy of all expenditure,” say the teachers.
notes: gatimattva literally 'having movement/motion' (of money, i.e. mobility); no sense added. pratīkāra = remedy (glossary). The quoted sentence has no stated subject noun; '[The ally]' is understood.

hindi: “नहीं,” ऐसा कौटिल्य कहते हैं।
english: “No,” says Kautilya.

hindi: क्योंकि “मित्र और धन भूमि के लाभ से होते हैं”, पहले कहा गया है।
english: For “ally and money arise from the acquisition of land” has been said before.
notes: Refers back to unit 2. The printed 'bhavata ity' is bhavataḥ iti.

hindi: इसलिए भूमि में भोग वाला मित्र श्रेष्ठ है।
english: Therefore an ally of enjoyment in land is better.
notes: The closing iti of the conclusion is not rendered.

hindi: पुरुषों में भोग के बराबर होने पर पराक्रम, कष्ट सहने की क्षमता, अनुराग अथवा सब सेना का लाभ मित्र के कुल से विशेष है।
english: When enjoyment in men is equal, valour, endurance of hardship, attachment, or the acquisition of all troops [is] the distinction from the ally's family.
notes: mitra-kulāt (ablative) is obscure: 'the distinction arising from / in comparison with the ally's family' are both possible; rendered literally. kleśa-sahatva = being able to bear hardship. bala = troops.

words.gloss: the state of the object requested

hindi: धन में भोग के बराबर होने पर प्रार्थित-अर्थता, प्रचुरता, अल्प प्रयास और निरन्तरता विशेष है।
english: When enjoyment in money is equal, the state of the object requested, abundance, littleness of effort and continuity [are] the distinction.
notes: prārthita-arthatā is rendered literally ('state of [having] the requested object'); the sense (the object asked for being obtained) is not stated. alpa-prayasatā = 'having little effort'; ca joins the last item.

hindi: इस विषय में यह है।
english: In this matter there is this [verse].
notes: Formula introducing the verses that follow (units 38-49); '[verse]' is supplied because the verses follow in the next units.

hindi: नित्य, वश में रहने वाला, हल्के रूप से उठने वाला, पिता-पितामह का, महान् और द्वैधभाव से रहित — उत्कृष्ट मित्र छह गुणों वाला कहा जाता है।
english: Constant, controlled, of light rising, of father and grandfather, great, and without duplicity — an excellent ally is called one having six qualities.
notes: The six qualities are the six adjectives of line a and the first of line b, counted as nitya, vaśya, laghu-utthāna, pitṛ-paitāmaha, mahat, advaidhya. advaidhya = literally 'non-doubleness'. The iti sums up the list and is not rendered. sampanna as in unit 7.

words.gloss: having a connection built up before

hindi: जो प्रयोजन के बिना स्नेह से रक्षित होता है और जो रक्षा करता है, जिसका सम्बन्ध पहले से बढ़ाया गया है, वह मित्र नित्य कहा जाता है।
english: [The ally] which, apart from a purpose, is protected out of affection, and which protects, having a connection built up before — that ally is called constant.
notes: ṛte artham is taken as 'apart from a purpose (artha)', i.e. without regard to gain. praṇaya has two senses, 'affection' and 'request' (glossary 5.2 has 'request' for Book 5): 'out of affection' chosen here, 'on request' is the alternative. upacita = built up, accumulated. The relatives yat ... yat have no stated noun; '[The ally]' is understood from mitram.

words.gloss: of all, varied and great enjoyment

hindi: वश में रहने वाला तीन प्रकार का कहा जाता है: सर्व, चित्र और महान् भोग वाला; एक ओर से भोग करने वाला, दोनों ओर से, और दूसरा सब ओर से भोग करने वाला।
english: The controlled [ally] is called threefold: of all, varied and great enjoyment; enjoying from one side, from both sides, and the other enjoying from all sides.
notes: Obscure. The compound sarva-citra-mahā-bhogam is read as a dvandva of three kinds of bhoga (all, varied, great) matching trividham; line b gives three kinds by direction of enjoyment, but with ubhayataḥ standing without bhogī and ca-aparam ('and the other') before sarvato-bhogi, the mapping between the two lines is uncertain. Rendered literally; gram of the compound is a guess.

words.gloss: retreating to its fort and forest

hindi: लेने वाला अथवा देने वाला भी अथवा — शत्रुओं में हिंसा से जीता है; मित्र नित्य, वश में न रहने वाला, और उसके दुर्ग और वन में हटने वाला।
english: Taking, or even giving, or — [it] lives among enemies by violence; an ally constant, uncontrolled, and retreating to its fort and forest.

text_flags.why: possible: the dot suggests a compound, but dātṛ and api are two words (sandhi dātry api)

notes: The second vā closes the alternatives (taking, or giving) and is rendered 'or' before the dash; the subject of jīvati is not stated. tad-durga-aṭavy-apasārin: apasārin = going away / retreating; the compound could also be 'having its fort and forest as place of retreat' (cf. glossary apasāra = place of retreat in 10.2). The sentence is elliptic.

hindi: जो दूसरी ओर से विग्रह में पड़ा हुआ है अथवा हल्के व्यसन वाला ही है, और उपकार के लिए सन्धि करता है, वह मित्र वश में रहने वाला, अस्थिर है।
english: [The ally] which is assailed from another quarter, or indeed has a light calamity, and makes a treaty for help — that ally is controlled, unstable.
notes: vigṛhīta (vi-√grah) = one on whom war has been made / involved in hostility; rendered 'assailed'. sandhatte: object not stated ('makes a treaty [with him]'). vyasana = calamity (glossary 8.1). Order of vā and eva: 'light calamity indeed, or'.

words.gloss: changeable toward the one to be helped

hindi: यह मित्र, एक अर्थ से बँधा हुआ, तब उपकार्य के प्रति परिवर्तनशील और मित्रभावी, आपत्ति में द्वैधभाव से रहित है।
english: Bound by a single purpose, then changeable toward the one to be helped, and ally-natured, this ally is without duplicity in adversity.
notes: Obscure. upakārya-vikārin read 'changing in regard to the one to be helped' (upakārya = one who is to be helped); the sense 'turning against' is not stated. mitra-bhāvin: bhāvin = having the nature of / tending to be; 'ally-natured'. atha rendered 'then'. Word order of the Hindi follows the English.

words.gloss: from being common with the enemy

hindi: मित्र-भाव से मित्र ध्रुव है, शत्रु के साथ साझा होने से चल; किसी का नहीं, उदासीन; दोनों में वह दोनों के भाव वाला है।
english: From ally-nature the ally [is] firm, from being common with the enemy, shaky; [the one] of no one [is] neutral; of the two, that [one] is of both-nature.
notes: Verbless clauses with the copula supplied. na kasyacit udāsīnam: 'neutral [belongs] to no one'. dvayor ubhaya-bhāvi tat is read 'of the two (parties), that one is ubhaya-bhāvin'. Technical names of the classes: mitra-bhāvin, śatru-sādhāraṇa, udāsīna, ubhaya-bhāvin; the ones in units 45-48.

hindi: जो मित्र विजिगीषु का अमित्र है, छिपाव में चला गया है, अथवा उपकार में लगा नहीं है, अथवा असमर्थ है, वह उपकार न करने वाला है।
english: The ally which is an enemy of the conqueror, gone to concealment, or not engaged in helping, or incapable — that is non-helping.
notes: antardhitāṃ gatam: 'gone to concealment' (antardhitā, feminine abstract), taken literally. The list of unhelpful kinds is read as alternatives: enemy of the conqueror gone into concealment / not engaged in helping / incapable. vijigīṣu = the conqueror (glossary 6.2).

hindi: जो मित्र दूसरे के प्रिय, अथवा रक्षणीय, पूजनीय, अथवा सम्बद्ध को ही अनुगृहीत करता है, क्योंकि वह शत्रु के साथ साझा है।
english: The ally who favours [one] dear to the other, or [one] to be protected, venerable, or indeed connected — for that [ally] is common with the enemy.
notes: parasya is 'of the other' (glossary 9.2: para = the other, not 'enemy'). The objects (priyam, rakṣyam, pūjyam, sambaddham) are neuter accusatives without stated noun; '[one]' supplied.
